items.response: LEAN TO 50 RPM DROP BELOW BEST POWER

items.condition: If IFR (or VFR in Class B, C, D airspace)

items.text: If failure occurs in VFR conditions, or VFR conditions are encountered after failure, continue flight under VFR and land as soon as practicable.
VFR Landing at a Controlled Field:
Remain outside or above Class D airspace until traffic flow determined.
Transmit intentions “in the blind” advising tower of aircraft type, position, altitude, and intention to land.
Enter pattern, report position “in the blind”, and watch for light signals from tower.
If failure occurs in IFR conditions, continue flight according to the following:

items.response: A – Assigned, V – Vectored, E – Expected, F – Filed

items.text: Altitude (highest of for the route segment being flown): (MEA)
items.response: M – Minimum IFR Altitude, E – Expected as Advised by ATC, A – Assigned by ATC

items.text: Descent for Approach: From enroute altitude upon reaching the IAF but not before: 1. Expect-further-clearance time (if given) 2. ETA as calculated from filed ETE

items.response: Return for Landing (to be followed by steady green)
Give way to other aircraft and continue circling
Taxi clear of runway in use
Return to starting point on airport

items.text: Alternating Red and Green — On Deck
Acknowledge all light signals by flashing landing light and/or rocking wings.
When the condition of the landing surface is in doubt, it is recommended that the landing gear remain in the up position.
If oil temp shows rise, engine failure imminent:
If oil temp does not show rise:
Fly using Turn-and-Slip Indicator, Altimeter, and Airspeed Indicator
If the gear cannot be lowered successfully, proceed with the emergency procedures for the appropriate gear malfunction.
• If an unsafe gear indication existed and the gear have been successfully lowered, do not attempt to raise the gear. • Raising the gear after a malfunction could cause further damage.
If the gear fails to extend, a wheels-up landing can be made on either hard or soft ground; however a hard surface is preferable. To accomplish a gear-up landing, proceed as follows:

sections.title: Landing with One Main Gear Retracted

items.text: Gear up landing is preferred to a landing with one main gear retracted.
Have gear position checked visually by another pilot or by the tower.

If verified that one gear is not fully extended and an attempt to retract is unsuccessful, execute a normal approach with full flaps and power on to reduce landing speed, carrying the wing slightly lower on the down-and-locked side.
Touch down smoothly on the down-and-locked gear. Hold the opposite wing up with aileron as long as possible after the nosewheel touches down.
When wingtip strikes the ground, apply maximum opposite brake pressure.
Should the nose gear fail to extend fully:
Make gentle pitching oscillations to swing nose gear into down position.
When landing, smoothly apply full forward stick to maintain pressure on the nose gear.
Should the nose gear fail to extend:
After touching main wheels down, hold the nose up as long as possible with full nose-down elevator trim and full backstick.
Before the nose settles onto the ground:

sections.title: Landing with a Flat Main Tire

items.text: Hold airplane off flat tire as long as possible
Maintain directional control using good-tire brake

sections.title: Landing with a Flat Nose Tire

items.text: Hold nosewheel off ground as long as possible
